desc:
Two lists of half-open intervals [start, end) with integer endpoints are given: keep and remove. The interval [s, e) covers every real number x with s ≤ x < e, and start < end always holds. Inside each list the intervals are sorted and disjoint: each one starts strictly after the previous one ends.

Return the parts of keep that are not covered by remove, as a sorted list of half-open intervals. Report the pieces maximally: each piece is a connected stretch, and no piece is empty.

keep   = [[0, 10], [12, 20]]
remove = [[2, 4], [8, 14], [18, 19]]
result = [[0, 2], [4, 8], [14, 18], [19, 20]]

Here [0, 10) loses [2, 4) and [8, 10), and [12, 20) loses [12, 14) and [18, 19).
hints: Taking each interval of keep and testing all intervals of remove is O(n · m). Both lists are sorted, so a pointer into remove never has to go backwards.
Work on one interval [s, e) of keep at a time with a moving left edge cur = s. Walk through the removal intervals that start before e.

For a removal interval [rs, re) overlapping the window: if rs > cur output [cur, rs); then set cur = max(cur, re). After the loop output [cur, e) if cur < e. Do not advance the removal pointer past an interval that may also cover the next keep interval.
editorial: Process the keep intervals in order. For the current [s, e) keep a cursor cur that marks the start of the not-yet-resolved part, initially s. First skip removal intervals that end at or before cur; they affect nothing from here on, because later keep intervals start even further right.

Then scan removal intervals that start before e. A removal interval beginning after the cursor leaves a surviving piece [cur, rs); in every case the cursor jumps to max(cur, re), the end of the removed stretch. If the cursor reaches e the interval is fully consumed. Otherwise the tail [cur, e) survives. The removal pointer is left on the last interval examined, since it can extend into the next keep interval.

Pieces from different keep intervals are separated by the strict gaps in keep, and pieces within one interval are separated by non-empty removed stretches, so the output is automatically in canonical form. Every pointer move is permanent, so the running time is O(n + m).
